========================================================================================
SPEEDUP FROM THE MATRIX ESSAY (decoded)
========================================================================================

WHAT THE ~220 LINES CLAIM
  1. Correlate CHANGE in d with CHANGE in P, not digit strings of x,y.
  2. If d' = d + Delta (mod N):   P' = P + Delta*G
     If d' = 2d + 1:              P' = 2P + G
     If d' = a*d + b:             P' = a*P + b*G
  3. If only a few Delta values repeat, PRECOMPUTE those Delta*G once.
     Then each matrix row costs ONE point addition, not a full d*G.
  4. Keep working points in Jacobian form (avoid inverses every step).
  5. Convert to printed decimal ONLY when checking:
        0.<x/p 156 digits>.<y/p 156 digits>
     That is the 'right side of the decimal place' — DISPLAY of x/p,y/p.

WHAT IS NOT A SPEEDUP
  - Adding/multiplying the printed decimal digit strings of x and y
  - Nested constructions like (x.(y/p))/p as an EC replacement
  - Any L(P) with L(P+Q)=L(P)+L(Q) mod N  (that IS the discrete log)

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A) FACTORADIC LEAD MATRIX — recurring Delta = da * k!
   (this is where unique deltas stay small enough to precompute)
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  lead steps = 49
  unique da  = 10  values={0: 5, 1: 9, 2: 13, 3: 7, 4: 6, 5: 3, 6: 3, 7: 1, 8: 1, 13: 1}
  unique |Delta_lead| = 43

  PRECOMPUTE BUDGET (lead walk):
    For each active order k, store T = k!*G once.
    Observed da in {0,1,2,...,13} — at most ~14 multiples of T needed,
    or just add T repeatedly da times (da is tiny).
    Full-key jumps between puzzles: 81 unique huge Deltas — NO precompute win.
    Lead climb inside an order class: SMALL da — YES precompute win.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
B) TIMING DEMO — full d*G vs incremental P + da*(k!*G)
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  plateau max_k=21 puzzles=[67, 68, 69, 70]
  precompute T=k!*G once (excluded from incremental loop cost above setup)
  time first full d0*G           = 0.169 ms
  time 3 separate full di*G = 0.499 ms
  time 3 lead increments     = 0.282 ms
  ratio full/incremental (lead ops) ~ 1.8x

  NOTE: lead-only increment is the cheap recurring piece the matrix exposes.
  Remainder (d - a*k!) still changes and still needs its own rule/walk.
  The essay's win is: replace FULL scalar muls with adds when Delta repeats.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
C) FULL INCREMENTAL WALK with decimal PRINT (right-of-point = x/p and y/p)
   P_{i+1} = P_i + Delta*G ; print 0.<x/p>.<y/p>
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  verified incremental adds: 81/81

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
D) SCALAR RULE -> POINT RULE (from the essay)
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  d+1     -> P+G
  d-1     -> P-G
  2d      -> 2P          (EC double)
  2d+1    -> 2P+G        (double then add G)
  3d+c    -> 3P+cG
  d+Delta -> P+Delta*G   (precompute Delta*G if Delta repeats)

  Printed form after each EC op:
    0.<right: x/p>.<right: y/p>
  The speedup is on the EC op count (left: d-side recurrence),
  not on arithmetic of the digit strings to the right of the decimal.

========================================================================================
BOTTOM LINE
========================================================================================
  Right side of the decimal = DISPLAY of field elements as x/p and y/p.
  Speedup = fewer EC scalar muls via recurring Delta/(a,b) from the matrix.
  Jacobian internally; 0.<x/p>.<y/p> only at check/print time.
  Nested (x.(y/p))/p was a formatting digression — not the essay's speedup.
